issue_context.title: Element.classList.toggle does not work in IE
issue_context.body:
Attach (recommended) or Link to PDF file here:
https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/web/viewer.html

Configuration:
- Web browser and its version: IE (any version)
- Operating system and its version: Windows 8/10
- PDF.js version: 2.0.943
- Is a browser extension: No

Steps to reproduce the problem:
1. Execute document.getElementsByTagName('body')[0].classList.toggle('test') on the Internet Explorer console

What is the expected behavior? (add screenshot)
Should add or remove a class to an element.

What went wrong? (add screenshot)
Throws an "invalid calling object" error

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11443206/51264361-3bcff880-19ae-11e9-9681-76a8b5d1aa05.png)

review_comments:
Arguable, but would it have been work calling the original function?  The main benefit would be that if the underlying implementation to `toggle` changes, then this never needs to change.  i.e.:

```js
return originalDOMTokenListToggle.call(this, token);
```
I think that's essentially what we had before this fix and it didn't work in IE. Since this is only a polyfill for IE and toggle functionality is trivial, I don't think we need to change this.

The original call was this:

```js
return originalDOMTokenListToggle(token);
```

My suggestion, which also fixes the problem in IE, is this:

```js
return originalDOMTokenListToggle.call(this, token);
```

It's ultimately not a big deal since the issue is now fixed.

Ah, I see. The diff in this patch is actually old; in the current code it's minimized to https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/blob/master/src/shared/compatibility.js#L110-L113. In the current code I don't think calling the original function is really possible anymore since that one doesn't support the `force` parameter, so then we would need to special-case it and get back to the code in this diff. Indeed it doesn't really matter too much since it's a working polyfill and it will probably be removed once we drop IE support in a later major release anyway.
Seems like a moot point then, thanks for calling that out!
